utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. May we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For the Prosecution, Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, senior trial attorney, and I'm actually expecting Mr. Dan Saxon who I think is on his way already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The accused, Dr. Vojislav Seselj in person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back to this later. The purpose of a meeting under Rule 65 bis, the so-called Status Conference, is to find out what are the actual problems of this case, how the case's development, or as it reads in the Rule as such, "A Trial Chamber or permanent Trial Chamber Judge shall convene a Status Conference within 120 days of the Initial Appearance of the accused and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference to organise exchanges between the parties so as to ensure expeditious preparation for trial, to review the status of his or her case and to allow the accused the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of the accused." May I start with the latter point and ask you, are there any special health problems you would have?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask that we do not begin with the last point. I do have some health problems, but they are not the most important for me. Could you leave those matters regarding my health condition for the end, as envisaged by the rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The order of the proceedings are decided by the Judge. May I ask you once again, do you have any health problems?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have serious health problems. My health problems are of a psychological nature. I cautioned you of these problems at the Initial Appearance. I repeated them at the first Status Conference, and now this has developed into very serious mental suffering, and I insist that the Trial Chamber take appropriate measures to diminish or remove that suffering. Your judicial clothing and robes worn by the Prosecution and the Judges cause a great deal of disturbance for me. They cause a great deal of anguish. You promised that something would be done, and this was repeated at the Status Conference, but I still haven't received anything. I insist that you set a team of psychiatric experts who will examine whether your robes which are reminisce sent of the Roman Catholic inquisition whether they really do cause anguish. If the psychiatrists find that is not true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't want to hear these arguments another time. You have to accept that in the courtrooms of this world, different gowns are worn by counsel and Judges and so it is also in this Tribunal. You have to accept it and this is no reason. If you would have special health problems, please let us know. And if you have other reasons to believe that you have mental health problems, please let us know. And also, let us know whether they are new ones or whether they already existed at the alleged time when allegedly you, as we can see it in the indictment, and this is the submission by the Prosecution, have committed the crimes listed there. Is it your intention that a research of your mental state be conducted for the actual period of time, or also for the time when the alleged crimes were committed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Never in my life have I had any psychological problems. They arose exclusively for the reasons I have mentioned. I am not denying your right to wear the robes you're wearing. But for me, it is unacceptable that they should be reminiscent of the Roman Catholic inquisition. If you were to wear uniforms of the United Nations, that would not disturb me. If you were to wear judicial robes from Chinese, Japanese, Arabic traditions, I wouldn't mind. But this I find intolerable, and my own problems are linked to this. If I had at least received rules regulating this clothing, then maybe my suffering would have been at least somewhat mitigated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I believe nothing has to be added to the words of the Appeals Chamber calling your submissions frivolous once, and I don't want to enter into any discussion of this problem, as you believe is a problem. May I then continue with some other issues. The first is related to a minor mistake --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I give you the floor when I feel it appropriate. In the first Initial Appearance, I asked you for your name and address and so on. But I omitted to ask you explicitly, is it correct that part of your name is the doctor degree, and can you please tell us when and where you obtained this doctor degree.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The title of "doctor" is part of my name, and I acquired the title of doctor of law when, on the 25th of November, 1979, I defended my doctoral thesis at the law faculty of the university in Belgrade. I am a doctor of sciences. In Germany, that would be a doctorate of second degree. As far as I know, Germans have several levels, or a Ph.D. in among the British and the Americans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. In this context, another question, please, and of course you know, and it's still true, that you have the right to remain silent. Is it correct that you gave lectures at the University of Michigan in the past?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not true. And used an untruthful fact in your decision against which I lodged an appeal, and then they tried to return that appeal to me. I never held lectures at Michigan University. I visited that university only once in my life for three or four hours in 1978. The university in Michigan, I think it is in -- near Detroit, I visited their library and was looking for certain books at that library. I have never lectured at any American university, and that is just evidence that this Trial Chamber in its rulings relies on untruthful and unverified data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To verify this was the intention of my question. You have answered the question. I thank you. You stated that making reference to the Chamber's decision on the Prosecution motion for order appointing counsel to assist Vojislav Seselj with his defence, we issued an order of 9th of May. And as you know, all your letters related to this had been returned because they were either not in the formal way or they were belated. You got as an assistance a letter from the senior legal officer of the Appeals Chamber. It is not for me to discuss issues of the Appeals Chamber; however, the senior legal officer recalled that under Rule 73, whenever you want to move or appeal against any decision of this Chamber, you have to do this in the foreseen way and within seven days. Apparently, this was not the case, and this was the ruling of the Appeals Chamber. Under Rule 73, it reads: "Discussions and all motions without interlocutory appeal save certification by the Trial Chamber which may grant such certification if the decision involves an issue that would significantly affect the fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings or the outcome of the trial, and for which, in the opinion of the Trial Chamber, an immediate resolution by the Appeals Chamber may materially advance the proceedings." Is it correct, Dr. Seselj, that you never filed such request for certification?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my opinion that there's no sense in filing an appeal for certification to ask the Trial Chamber to -- to complain to the Trial Chamber about its own decision. I have 25 Rules of the Rules of Procedure which are in contradiction with the Statute of this Tribunal. I have submitted to the Appeals Chamber. It is not possible for a legal officer to communicate with me. The Appeals Chamber could have rejected my objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, we have heard this already in the past. I think you have called yourself once in your Initial Appearance "the best lawyer in the world." You would know yourself. But I know how difficult it is to work sometimes with our Rules. You were notified on the content of this Rule 73. You have these Rules in a language you understand. And therefore, you have, as all the other inmates in the Detention Unit or other accused before this Tribunal, to obey the Rules and to follow the Rules. We can't make an exception especially for you. So therefore, we have to state that you failed to request such a certification that might be granted in the interests of justice; and in addition, it was recalled by the senior legal officer that in case such a certification is granted by the Trial Chamber, then in addition, you would have to file within another seven days, as it reads in Rule 73 para C, Requests for certification shall be filed within seven days of the filing of the impugned decision. Where such decision is rendered orally, this time limit shall run from the date of the oral decision. If certification is given, a party may appeal to the Appeals Chamber within seven days of the filing of the decision to certify. So this would be a second -- a two-step approach. Twice seven days. Until now, you have failed. It's a long time ago since the 9th of May. However, I have to recall, and I'm quite sure that you're fully aware of this, under Rule 127, the Rules provide for the possibility of the variation of time limits. And there it reads: "Save as provided by paragraph C, a Trial Chamber may, on good cause being shown by motion, enlarge any time prescribed by under these Rules." So there would still the possibility for you under Rule 127 to show good cause why you failed to request the certification within seven days, and then the Trial Chamber would have to decide whether cause indeed has been shown or not, and then proceed. This would be the way, in case you would continue, to oppose that which has been decided by the Trial Chamber, and this is primarily that a standby counsel be assigned to you, that no doubt, you have the right to defend yourself, and in addition you have the right to appoint Defence counsel under Rule 44(A). I think this is absolutely clear from our decision, and you can read it there and re-examine it once again. So there is still a door open. If you want to proceed this way, please do so. But please, immediately and try to show good cause. Do you want to mention anything in this relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On the 26th of May, I filed to the Appeals Chamber of the International Tribunal 37 pages of my objection regarding your decision to appoint a standby counsel against the law. In that objection, I stated as a reason your failure to have jurisdiction. According to interlocutory appeals, certification is required in all cases accept when jurisdiction is being challenged. And in addition to that, the Trial Chamber also allows for questioning the legality of the Tribunal itself. There's a special decision in the Tadic case. So whenever jurisdiction is being challenged, I challenged your right to appoint a standby counsel. And according to your own Rules, no certification is required from the Trial Chamber, but the objection goes directly to the Appeals Chamber. And that is in question here, challenging jurisdiction. And as that is the case, I ask you to observe the provisions of your Rule 72 and to forward my motion directly to the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dr. Seselj, your letters were sent directly to the Appeals Chamber, and you received the answers from the Appeals Chamber. No doubt that a Trial Chamber can't interfere in the work of the Appeals Chamber. And therefore, our hands are bound. What I did was showing you a way how to come to this decision you apparently still want, but please, don't confuse two issues: The question whether or not to assign counsel against your will, but leaving you the right, the absolute right, to defend yourself, and the question of jurisdiction. This, of course, follows, and you mentioned it correctly, different rules. And therefore, please make a distinction yourself when you file a motion, and I emphasise it's not sufficient to write a letter "to whom it may concern" but file a motion as foreseen under the Rules in Section 6 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence. So therefore, in case you want to try and reopen the question of Defence counsel, you know now the way how to do it under Rule 127 and Rule 73 paragraph (B). Then let us stay for a moment with the question of Defence counsel. On the one-hand side, you stated, both in the Initial Appearance and in the further Initial Appearance, that you decided to defend yourself. On the other hand, I received today two powers of attorney authorising Maja Gojkovic, lawyer in Novi Sad, to act as your legal advisor. This was signed "The Hague, the 2nd of July, 2003." At the same time, you signed a power of attorney authorising Slavko Jerkovic, lawyer of Savi Glacevica [phoen] Street, number 28 in Belgrade as to act as my legal assistant in the case we have before us. The Rules provide under Rule 44 for the right to have counsel. May I ask you, shall we interpret your power of attorney related to Maja Gojkovic as such a proxy or power of attorney under Rule 44(A)?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I need to inform you that more than three months ago, I informed the Registrar of this Tribunal that Maja Gojkovic an attorney from Novi Sad will be my legal advisor, and Slavko Jerkovic, an attorney from Belgrade, my legal assistants. Then officials came, expert advisors of the Tribunal to discuss this with me orally. I provided the data for Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic. They had several contacts with them. Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic sent their powers of attorney two and a half months ago. Those same court officials should have come to see me to sign those powers of attorney. They didn't come and they no longer answered the telephone. Maja Gojkovic will be my legal advisor. She is already working in that capacity informally. And Slavko Jerkovic will be my legal assistant. They will be working in accordance with my instructions and my own concept of defence as I have determined it. Therefore, they do not have the authority of a legal Defence counsel. They cannot undertake any steps until I give them instructions to do so and permission to do so. What I wish to avoid, which is unfortunately the practice in this Tribunal, that when the accused appoints Defence counsel, then his destiny is entirely in the hands of the Defence counsel. I will be in charge of my own defence case. And Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic will assist me, and some 20 or so investigators who have already been engaged for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Rules are quite clear. You have the possibility either to defend yourself or to have counsel. And as we already have described in our decision of May this year, that notwithstanding that you prefer to take the right to self-representation, it would be possible, and it does not exclude - this is written in paragraph 29 of our decision - your right to obtain legal advice from counsel of your own choosing. This would be counsel, and this counsel would have to follow the Rules under 44(A) and would have to act under the same obligations and the same rights as it is for all the other counsel in this Tribunal. So it's your decision whether you want to defend yourself or together with counsel. And I have to correct you. It is not true that when you have an appointed counsel or assigned counsel, then you would be in the hands of these counsel. The counsel would act only in your interest and follow your advice. So may I ask you once again, you used terms not foreseen in the Statute. And I'm not aware why you explicitly used in two powers of attorney two different terms, once, "legal assistant" and in the other time "legal advisor." In which category shall these persons fall?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there's no need at all to raise that question again while this case lasts. For as long as it lasts, I will defend myself. A legal advisor has helped me hitherto. Already, for instance, in obtaining certain case law, studying certain legal issues and so on. As for the legal assistant, he heads the team of investigators that I have engaged, my intention being to find witnesses whereby I will be able to challenge all the counts in the indictment. So my decision remains the same, to defend myself. But my impression is that the whole Tribunal, you yourself and the Registry of this Tribunal, are endeavouring in every way to impose Defence counsel on me, even by proclaiming my legal advisor or legal assistants as Defence counsel. I will not have a Defence counsel. You can appoint hundreds of lawyers as standby attorneys; I will not collaborate with them, nor will I recognise any move that they make. You can leave me without a defence, but you cannot force me to agree to anyone defending myself except me. You can appoint anyone to act in my name. He can even change his name, take my name. But that is beyond my powers of control. My decision to defend myself is final, unequivocal, and there's nothing that can change it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber did otherwise, and it would be for you if you are not in agreement with our decision to take the necessary measures. I already indicated what these would be. And it's now for you to take action or not. If you wouldn't take action within the next seven days, this standby counsel would be assigned to you. As for the two other persons, I have to inform you that the lawyer/client privilege foreseen under Rule 97 is not available for these persons before they are accepted under Rule 44(A). And they have to be accepted by the Registrar, not by the Trial Chamber. So therefore, please act in this respect vis-a-vis the Registrar as foreseen in Rule 44. And the Registrar will then decide whether or not these persons can be seen as counsel in the sense of Rule 44 and whether or not you would enjoy this client/counsel privilege or not. So unfortunately, I didn't get a clear answer from your side related to the question whether you want to regard these persons -- you want these persons as explicit counsel as foreseen or not, because one thing should be quite clear from the outset: You can't give to the public the impression if you would defend yourself; and on the other hand, by the back door, through the back door, let you defend by counsel not appearing. So you know the steps you would have to take if you so want. It's up to you. May I now ask the Prosecution, are there, from the Prosecution side, any submissions related to disclosure issues especially?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution is continuing its trial preparations, basically contacting and recontacting witnesses already identified and potential further witnesses. The Prosecution has to clarify the scope of the anticipated testimony, in particular, the possible protective measures needed. When this process is concluded, and also as far as it is developing, we will file protective measures motion. One of them in the near future. And the Prosecution has also the intention to file at a later stage the -- a motion requesting the admission of crime-based evidence according to Rule 92 bis, but we will need some time to do this, in particular, we have to clarify with the Defence or with the accused which matters are actually in dispute when it comes to crime-based. The Prosecution is also at the moment identifying exhibits that will be used at trial; however, this process is also not coming to an end as long as we don't know which are the facts in dispute and which are not. The Prosecution's actually awaiting the standby counsel, or rather a decision of the Appeals Chamber to standby counsel, before submitting suggestions to the accused pursuant to Rule 65 ter (E) for possible admissions of background facts as well as an agreement on matters which are not in dispute and which matters are contested. But we have actually -- we will only submit that when the situation regarding Defence counsel is clarified. In relation to disclosure, actually my colleague Dan Saxon who deals with this matter and I would like to refer to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Today, basically I have two matters to clarify with the Trial Chamber. First of all, since the arrest and detention of Dr. Seselj, the Prosecution has begun defining criteria for locating and identifying material that would be subject to disclosure to Dr. Seselj pursuant to Rule 68. And that process is ongoing and will be ongoing for the length of these proceedings obviously. However, we are prepared today to begin disclosure of materials to Dr. Seselj under Rule 68. Most of the material is material already in the public domain, but a portion of it is not. It is material that is not in the public domain. And we have highlighted these differences in our disclosure package so it will be clear to the accused. We have prepared a receipt in the language of the accused and in English so that the accused will be able to see exactly what it is we are providing him. All of these materials that we have prepared for disclosure this afternoon are in the language of the accused. So he should have no trouble reading them or, in the case of several videotapes, watching them and understanding them. So with the Court's leave, I would ask the Registrar either now or at a later date -- or at a later moment during this hearing to provide this package and a receipt for the accused's signature to the accused, along with these videotapes. That is the first matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to assist, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let us wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May it please be immediately handed over to Dr. Seselj that we know whether Dr. Seselj is prepared to accept this or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why shouldn't I be prepared to accept this? So far, I have accepted all Court documents in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm more than happy to know that you would accept this. But let's please proceed in the way foreseen under the Rules --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With satisfaction, Your Honour. Very pleased. But only in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There are two copies of the receipt there. One of them is for Dr. Seselj, and we would ask that one of them be returned to us, to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dr. Seselj, only to be on the safe side, I take it that you're in possession of an audio and videoplayer provided to you by the Registrar. Is this correct? That you are able to review these videotapes you just received?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. But unfortunately, I just received it five days ago, so I haven't had time to look through all the videotapes that I received on the 17th of March, if I remember correctly. So that in the course of the next ten days, I will be able to take a look at all that material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Please, let me take the opportunity to recall that in the accompanying letter, it reads that you would have to renew a request after one month if you then still need this audio or videoplayer. Let it please be not forgotten. But I have interrupted the Prosecution. Mr. Saxon, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has also already identified some material that is disclosable to the accused, Dr. Seselj, under Rule 68. However, that material is in the English language. Again, we will wait until the final resolution of the matter of standby counsel before we decide or make an effort to disclose that material as well. In future disclosures under Rule 68, if we have the resources to do it and the amount is not too voluminous, we will try as we did on this instance to provide letters and receipts in the language of the accused. We will make our best effort, however, that is contingent on the language resources that are available to the Office of the Prosecutor at the time. Your Honour, the final point that I would make this afternoon regarding disclosure pursuant to Rule 68, the Prosecution would like to, as much as possible, engage the Defence and the Trial Chamber in the disclosure process so that this can be a collaborative effort to make sure that it is as efficient and as effective as possible. So in that light, with the Trial Chamber's leave, the Prosecution intends to file, perhaps on a bimonthly basis or trimonthly basis reports of the Prosecution concerning its compliance with the rules of disclosure, Rule 66 and Rule 68. That way, we will be able to engage all the parties in this process and keep all the parties fully informed in the disclosure activities of the Prosecution, including the kinds of criteria, search criteria, that the Prosecution is using to locate and identify potentially exculpatory material for the Defence in this case. And we hope to file our first report in the very near future, probably later this month, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this submission. May I ask you, Dr. Seselj, you're aware of the problems emanating from the fact that a huge number of documents, amounting to thousands of documents, would have to be translated. But my question is, is English a language you understand insofar as you could read the content in principle?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I cannot in this trial avail myself of the use of English. My knowledge of English is sufficient to be able to contact with the prison guards and possibly with the physician, and that's all. I am not able to enter into any legal discussions in English, nor am I able to professionally elaborate a legal text in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I then ask, what about Ms. Maja Gojkovic, is she able to understand and speak English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The same goes for the second person mentioned in your documents, and this would be Mr. Slavko Jerkovic, is he able to read and/or speak English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not for the purposes of the trial. Either Maja Gojkovic or Slavko Jerkovic, their knowledge is not sufficient to be able to use the language for trial purposes in these proceedings in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You should be aware, and you have the time to read Rule 44, that a counsel shall be considered qualified to represent a suspect or accused if the counsel satisfies the Registrar that the counsel is admitted to the practice of law in a state, or as a university professor of law, and speaks one of the two working languages of the Tribunal. This would be English or French. So please take this into account when you decide on counsel of your own choosing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why you keep insisting on this question of counsel of my own choosing when I am never going to have a counsel in this trial. And I don't know in what way I can express my thoughts because what I'm saying doesn't seem to be understandable to you. Perhaps the problem is in the interpreters. I don't know where the problem lies. I am never going to have a counsel here of any kind, and if you try to impose one on me, I'm not going to recognise him. I will have no contact with anybody like that. I insist that I defend myself. That is my right pursuant to the Statute and the European Declaration on Human Rights, the universal declaration on human rights and I don't understand why you keep insisting upon this question of counsel and raising the issue in that way. It's my impression that you wish to cause an incident here. You want to make me lose my patience, to commit an act that I do not want to commit. That is my impression. I don't know why you're doing that. There is no Defence counsel. I am my sole legal counsel here, and that decision is unequivocal. And I can guarantee with my very life that I will stand by that decision, and I guarantee it with my life. There is no Defence counsel in this Court for me, and there never will be. Now, as far as the material is concerned in English, Your Honour, I am saving money for you and the Tribunal. You won't have to pay a Defence counsel for me, an attorney for me. And therefore I assume that you can use those funds as resources to ensure the translation of documents into the Serbian language for me. It's cheaper, as far as I can assess, and I have had occasion to ask other accused, it's cheaper to engage ten translators rather than an attorney, an official attorney, as far as the funds of the Tribunal are concerned. Or you can pay more. There are donors of yours. So it's not my problem that your financial resources are restricted. Perhaps I am guilty of something that you ascribe to me, but you are going to have to prove that and I don't how you're going to do that. But I can't be to blame for your financial restrictions and I don't even want to think of the subject of money and fact that you don't have enough money. Don't burden me with that. I have other problems to worry about in my life. However every document, each and every document, must be translated into the Serbian language otherwise it is unacceptable to this Tribunal. If I don't see the document in Serbian, the document will not be allowed to exist as far as you're concerned and you're aware of that Your Honour. You were a Judge of the Supreme Court of Germany, as far as I understand. And you know that there are some limits in the mistreatment of the accused. Everything must be in the Serbian language. Now how you're going to do that and garbage it, that's up to you. But I have never refused to accept any document given to me in the Serbian language. I received and took over everything that was submitted to be in Serbian and signed for it except when a former legal advisor contacted me and writes letters to me, senior legal officer. I can't understand that. Although I have a Ph.D., I can't understand that a legal officer can contact with me in that way at all. I am here on a footing of equality in this trial. I am equal to the Prosecutor legally speaking until I leave here, and then you can tie me up and that's another matter. But while we're in this courtroom, we are completely equal. We are on a footing of equality and I wish to have that remain so to the end. So everything must be translated for me into Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm convinced that you perfectly well understood the message that is laid done in Rule 44, and I don't want to enter into a discussion of this question because it's for the Registrar to answer this question and not for the Trial Chamber. So let's leave it for the moment with this. May I ask the Prosecution, are there any other issues from your side you want to raise today?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask you, any other issues from your side you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have prepared 11 issues for this Status Conference here today, and I hope you'll have the patience to hear me out. The first question relates to my complaint with respect to the indictment. And this was tabled on the 18th of April. There was some problems over its reception the photocopy machine wasn't working during the weekend. Monday was a Dutch holiday, and this was filed and listed on the 22nd of April. The Trial Chamber was given a deadline of two months to state its views with respect to my submission, and I submitted the submission with respect to Rule 72. I questioned the authority and competence and jurisdiction with respect to that Rule, and I also challenged the formal defects in the form of the indictment. After one and a half months, once again, some legal counsellor tried to give me back my motion, and his explanation was that it was longer than ten pages. My motion totalled 116 pages. I said, Your Honour, at the last Status Conference that I was already writing my complaint with respect to the indictment, that it might number several hundred pages. You said that it couldn't be longer than so many pages, and I was able to reduce it to 116 pages and it could not have been shorter than that. Now my complaint to the indictment is my absolute right which nobody can take away from me following the Rules of Procedure first, and secondly as far as I know, there is no legal system in the world in which that right is not absolute, that the accused can lodge his complaints with respect to the indictment, which is what I did. However, it takes up more pages than are prescribed by the President of the Tribunal. The instructions given by the President of the Tribunal as a legal act does not rely on the Rules of Procedure at all and Evidence. The President of the Tribunal does not enjoy the right to restrict my right to table a complaint with respect to the indictment. I could have written it out on 1.000 pages. That is my right. If the Prosecution could send me six files of documents together with my indictment and twice the number of videocassettes that I received on the 17th of March, then I assume that I can write out what I say to cover 116 pages because I didn't choose all the umpteen files and binders that the Prosecution used, and there is no document in all those binders that can prove the indictment. But that's their affair. It's their ballast. It was your duty to respond to my complaint to the indictment to rule. You accept it or you don't accept it. I expected you to reject it straight away, but it was up to you to respond in one way or another. As the Trial Chamber, you cannot fail to respond to my submission and just say that it was too long. If you say today that you're not going to give a ruling, then pursuant to Rule 72 I have the right without your go ahead to complain to the Appeals Chamber in that regard because it is the lack of jurisdiction in granting this agreement or ruling or filing of a motion and complaint. I am fully conscious of the reasons for which the Trial Chamber does not wish to state its views because I challenge the competence of the Tribunal with respect to Vojvodina. There was no war in Vojvodina. And you want to us to prolong this process of statement of views. The Rules are not of a legal nature. They can of a political nature. However a Tribunal could not accept having political rulings of this kind. Now, with regard to competence and jurisdiction, I looked at the joint enterprise, and there is no grounds for that in the Statute as well, joint criminal enterprise. In article 7(1) or 7(3). It is something that has been brought up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we won't go into the details of the indictment. This is not the purpose of a Status Conference. I only want to recall, and apparently following your submissions, you're fully aware that there are these limitations related to the length of motions, and it is as easy as that that you only ask for leave to file a longer motion if need may be, if only you show good cause. And this has not been done by you in the past related to all the documents. And therefore, you are treated like all the other inmates in the Detention Unit. The documents are returned to you. It is for you to ask for leave for an extension of this page limitation, and then the Trial Chamber in its composition of three Judges will decide. It's absolutely easy, and I know that you have understood this very well. Are there any other problems?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that. But Your Honour I'm not going to abide by that because I insist upon the fact that the President of the Tribunal doesn't have the right to do so, to give instructions which will restrict my absolute rights or to interpret them restrictively, and I'm going to continue along those lines. Let me tell you this: I am ready to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me immediately answer. Then you have to take the consequences if you don't want to follow the rules and the guidelines. That's all I have to say to this. Other problems?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also wish to say that I am ready for that, to write my motions one page longer every time, and then at the end of the trial, you can say that they were all rejected because of their length, the length of my motions. And now something else: Your Honour, I have established that the Rules of Procedure and Evidence in 25 of the Rules go directly against the provisions of the Statute, and I'm going to show you this very quickly. The question of status --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is not the appropriate time to do so. That's not the purpose of a Status Conference, and it was on purpose that I quoted directly from the Rules what is the purpose of a Status Conference. If you want to challenge the validity of one of the Rules, please do so in writing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do that with pleasure, but I have not done so so far because according to the Rules, it is provided that only the Judges and Secretary can put forward motions for change in the Rules of Procedure. I think that this is something that should be done urgently because the Defence counsel or rather the accused must be set on a footing of equality with the Prosecution. But if you insist upon that, I can give this idea up for the time being, but I'd just like to draw your attention that I noted down all these 25 points in my complaint to your decision to impose a standby counsel for me. So if you're interested, you will be able to read it there. And I am convinced that anything I write down will remain in writing as a record in due course for people who are going to study this trial in a hundred years' time. The next issue I wish to raise is my being ignored by the Prosecution. I have come here of my own free will. I have been in prison for four and a half months now and the Prosecution has not wanted to have an official talk to me. They are running away from me like the plague. However, after the last Status Conference, Madam Del Ponte did call me into her office and asked me whether I wished to talk and I said, "Well, why aren't you recording the conversation?" And she said, "I thought we could talk privately." And I said, "We can talk privately about the weather or literature, not serious questions." And afterwards, there was no contact whatsoever. I was already to provide valuable information to the OTP about some war crimes and their perpetrators. I also wanted to testify how Zoran Djindjic the former Prime Minister was involved in these crimes because Ljubisa Mauzer was the greatest criminal in Republika Srpska and president of the party, and I think that Mauzer -- that the OTP knows who Mauzer is. Unfortunately in the meantime, Djindjic was killed. So this has been placed -- But I have serious information interesting to the OTP of the case of Nebojsa Colic who stole a factory and so on and the involvement of Milo Djukanovic, the Prime Minister of Montenegro, et cetera. I have reliable sources and they tell me that their liquidation is being prepared so it would be a good idea for you to hurry up and me to give you that information while the people are still alive. And you seem to be running away from me as if I have the plague or I am suffering from some infectious disease or something of the like. Now, on several occasions, we have mentioned another subject here, the question of language. And in your ruling signed by you, Your Honour, I can see that you refer to people who are not in any way professionals when it comes to the Serbo-Croatian language. So I have done my best to bring into Court here today and to give you one of my books, the ideology of Serb nationalism, where I deal with the problem on the basis of the top quality scientific research that is done to show you what the problem is all about. The problem is not about the fact that I couldn't understand something if I made the effort to do so, but that in the artificial Croatian variation, they are thinking up new words every day to make that language be as different as possible from Serbian which is the source language. And in 1850 the Croats gave up their language --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have heard already your submissions on this question, and we answered this by motion. And if you have problems with this, the Appeals Chamber is the adequate body to give you the answer. It stands how it is, and we have reliable sources to proceed this way. Any other questions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there are, but I insist that you ask members of the Registry to accept this and that it become part of the Court file because this book will be important for you for these entire proceedings. I hope you will not avoid this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... one of these mainly three variants of one of the same language, and we discussed in previous cases this question exhaustively. And the matter is hereby resolved. So if you want to turn to another issue, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you're avoiding to consider this question more seriously, I shall move on to another problem. Your Honour, I have never received two documents that you personally promised me, and those are the rules regarding the robes of the Judges and the United Nations agreement with the host country. In the minutes of the Status Conference and the Initial Appearance, you can find that you yourself promised me those documents. These are all minor matters, and I'll deal with them very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can answer immediately. May I ask the usher, please, to hand over to the -- to Dr. Seselj the document, the host country agreement. But as I stated earlier, you will not receive a solution of your problems related to visa questions. And I stated already earlier, there's no impediment, no obstacle at all that your relatives can come to The Hague and visit you in the Detention Unit. This is not a question emanating from the host country agreement. This goes without saying. As regards the robes, you discussed -- you touched upon this issue already earlier, and I'm tired of hearing the same repetitive story, so please turn to the next issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you're tired, we can have a break, but your fatigue cannot be an argument in these proceedings because I'm threatened with 14 life sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I stated I don't want to hear any longer any comments from your side related to the robes and gowns worn by officials of this Tribunal. Please proceed with other issues.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have insisted several times in writing that I be provided the transcripts of the Initial Appearance here and of the first Status Conference in the Serbian language. This is still not been served on me. I insist that this be provided because I cannot participate in a trial unless all transcripts are provided, and if I'm unable to use those transcripts for preparations for my Defence. For the present, I still remember well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you once again. It becomes a vicious circle. In the moment, you have a counsel or whatever you would call this person, legal assistant or legal advisor, the second is the specific term used in another case, then you would have access immediately to the transcripts, the transcripts are provided under the Rules and under the Statute in the languages of -- in the official languages of this Tribunal. This is English and French. On the other hand, you have the possibility to review the videos taken from these Status Conferences, and there should be no doubt that if you so want, you get these videos and then you can follow what has been said there. May I ask you in this context, is it correct that you were offered a laptop, but you refused to take this laptop as a tool assisting not only you, but also the parties and all the staff members of this Tribunal, especially the interpreters having sometimes enormous difficulties with your handwriting? Is it correct that such a laptop was offered to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the videotapes of the Initial Appearance and the Status Conferences, I don't mind having them. But I'm afraid that I can only follow what I said in the Serbian language. I don't know what happens to the interpretations on videotapes. If there's a technical solution to that, then the videotapes can -- I can use them just as I would use transcripts on condition they're in Serbian. As regards the laptop, this is something that you offered me at the last Status Conference as far as I remember, and I refused it. The accused addresses the Court originally by hand and original Court documents are written documents. Unfortunately, I'm not prepared for any modernisation. All documents have to be supplied in hard copy. If we're talking about evidence, they can be on videotapes. I assume that this is all evidence on videotapes and not documents. As regards my own filings, they will all be written by hand. I'm always at the disposal of the Court translators to help them read any word they may find difficulty with. I have plenty of time to be cooperative in that sense. But you will have to accept that until the end of these proceedings, I will continue to write everything by hand, and that all Court documents will have to be disclosed in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the problem related to the bookshelf, is it resolved in the meantime? Did you request this on the basis of a Zahtev form?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did make an oral request, and the answer I received was that they would see. But it was never provided. I need this simply to keep the documents in order, and those documents are piling up quickly because I have whole piles of things, including books. But in order to be able to conduct my own Defence, I need this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, we need not enter into these discussions. It's absolutely clear, but a prerequisite is a written request. This Zahtev form as I learned from the Detention Unit management, if you fill in this form, you will get immediately the bookshelf. Another issue, please, if you have.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as that is concerned, I have exhausted the questions I had planned for today, except if you allow me I would just like to say two sentences in connection with what has been said by the representative of the Prosecution. The representative of the Prosecution is raising the problem of documents, and he is linking that with the imposition of a standby Defence counsel. The Prosecution must not act in that way. The Prosecution must perform its duties regardless of that matter. And the Prosecution must not waste time, precious time, with respect to interpretation because sooner or later, these things will have to be translated and nothing will change in that respect. And I would like to say to you, Your Honour, in response to one of my first questions, you referred to the position of the Appeals Chamber which has nothing to do with the subject that I raised here. The position of the Appeals Chamber has to do with my request for your disqualification, and not regarding the motion that you referred to in connection with the Appeals Chamber. Those are two separate matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think you are aware that your request for disqualification, I have to refrain from any comments on this, was decided by the Bureau rejecting this as a frivolous motion. So nothing has to be added to this. Let me now turn to another point, only recently, in fact, immediately before I entered the courtroom, I received a document from Yugoslavia. I go into some details of this. And it was forwarded by the Embassy of Serbia and Montenegro and sent to us the 1st of July, 2003. I have to recall that during your Initial Appearance, the 26th of February, 2003, when asked whether the embassy should be informed on your deprivation of liberty according to Article 36 of the Vienna Convention, you answered: "No. I do not wish to have any contact with the consulate of the so-called Serbia and Montenegro. It is my conviction that in Serbia and Montenegro, Mafioso and criminals are in power and I do not wish any guarantees or any contact with them." On the other hand, we have a request for legal assistance from Serbia and Montenegro forwarded to us through the embassy. And this reads as follows, addressed to the International Tribunal: "Before the Special Department of the District court in Beograd, the investigation procedure is pending against the suspect Vojislav Seselj, born on October 11, 1954 in Sarajevo, son of the father Nikola for founded suspicion that he has committed the criminal act of association for enemy activity of the Article 136, paragraph 2 in connection with paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in concurrence with the criminal act of assassination of representatives of the highest federal authorities by instigation of the Article 122 in connection with the Article 23 of the Criminal Law of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, (currently: Basic Criminal Code). "It is necessary to interrogate in the capacity of the accused Vojislav Seselj who is situated in the Detention Unit in Scheveningen in The Hague, so you are most kindly to requested to approve the interrogation either in these premises or in the premises of the International Crime Tribunal for former Yugoslavia of Vojislav Seselj on the basis of the Criminal Procedure Code. "Besides the Summary Judge of this Court, Mr. Vucko Mircic, and the recorder, Ms. Novka Babovic, at such interrogation has been to be present also the Deputy Special Public Prosecuting Attorney Mr. Milan Radovanovic, as well as the suspect's Defence attorney, Attorney at Law, Mr. Slavko Jerkovic of Beograd-Zemun. "The suspect's Defence attorney advised us that the suspect demands for his interrogation to be recorded by the means of devices for sound and optical recording, to which he is entitled under the Article 179 of the Law on Criminal Procedure. In case you meet this request of ours, you are kindly requested as well to bear in mind that we shall provide a person and a device (camera) for taping the interrogation of the suspect subsequently. "We dare emphasise that the investigation in question is being introduced against further 45 persons, 24 persons of which are in confinement in the District Prison of Beograd, so that, for such reasons, urgent procedure is unavoidable. You are thus most kindly requested to consider approving the interrogation of Vojislav Seselj in the period from July 3 to July 17 taking into consideration our estimate that the hearing may last eight hours at the most. "Summary Judge of the Special Department, signed Vucko Mircic." So there seems to be a discrepancy. On the one-hand side you told us the 26th of February you do not want to have anything to do with representatives of Serbia and Montenegro. And on the other side, it is explicitly said here that your Defence attorney advised that a special way of interrogation should be conducted. May I ask you, therefore, are you prepared to undergo such a procedure of interrogation by authorities based on a request for legal assistance in criminal matters?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbian public, I have already made my position known, and I have authorised my lawyers, Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic to inform the investigating judge that I'm ready to be heard in their presence, not just Slavko Jerkovic but also Maja Gojkovic would come with the investigating judge and the Prosecutor. But I wrote a letter to the Registry of this Tribunal requesting that this Tribunal, because I'm here under your jurisdiction now, I think it is up to you to make sure that nobody can manipulate my status here for any purposes whatsoever. And that is why I would request that this Tribunal or the OTP provide a recording of my interrogation in the same way that they do it when they are interrogating suspects. And that after that interrogation, I be given the videotapes. If this Tribunal can guarantee that, I'm prepared and ready to talk to the investigating judge, with pleasure. There's only one thing that I fear, that somebody from the authorities in Belgrade should later on manipulate with my statements. What has happened hitherto, that the police hear a witness, then ministers then get hold of that and then manipulate with it. I wish to avoid that. But my assessment of the authorities remains the same. Now, if you will protect me and provide a recording of that interrogation and I'm given a tape of that interrogation, I'm ready to do that. I'm not avoiding it; on the contrary, I wish to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So we have got a clear answer from your side, that you would not make use of your fundamental right to remain silent as an accused in this affair pending against you in Belgrade. And therefore, you would be prepared to answer the questions put to you, and it would be only a question of how to proceed, how to protect your rights, and how technical to conduct this interview. Is this a correct statement, that you are prepared to answer these questions? Not to make use of your right, because it wouldn't make sense that we prepare this interrogation, and then later you tell us you make use of your right to remain silent.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is all correct, Your Honour, with the exception of one sentence. I have haven't yet been an accused over there. I'm just a suspect. So the status is a different one, and I'm saying this for the benefit of the public. So if you do provide these conditions for me, and you can guarantee that I will have the tape in my hands after the interrogation, I'm ready for any interviews. I have never used my right to silence as my defence especially as those accusations from Belgrade against me are fabrications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clear answer. I think it would be then for the Registrar and for the Prosecution to prepare the necessary measures if this request for assistance in criminal matters will be granted. And in the past, it was the policy to grant these requests. Any other issues to be raised? I can't see any. This concludes today's Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: adjourned at 5.06 p.m.
